title: Linked List in Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree's root and a linked list's head, determine if the linked list's elements form a downward path in the binary tree.
statement: Given a binary tree's root and a linked list's head, determine if the linked list's elements form a downward path in the binary tree. A downward path starts at any node and moves downward.
constraints: Match the linked-list values along a downward parent-to-child path that may start at any tree node.
Return whether every list node can be matched contiguously.
hints: Separate choosing a starting tree node from matching an already-started path.
The matcher compares current values and recursively follows either child with head.next.
At each tree node, try the matcher there, then search both subtrees for another start.
Every downward path has one starting node, and the two recursive layers enumerate every start and every child choice.
editorial: Use one recursion to match a fixed start and another to enumerate starting tree nodes. A match advances the list and exactly one tree edge per step; reaching the end of the list succeeds. The oracle independently builds a tree and explores explicit (tree node, list index) stacks from every node.

tests.explanation: Starting at the right child valued four gives the downward sequence four, two, eight.
No single downward branch contains the whole list in order.
